indicators.note: to succeed something is to come after it, so the second piece is placed behind the first

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.definitionFit: To doodle is to scribble idle pictures, so a person who doodles draws in an aimless way.

clue.text: Obligation created the first time uniform lost

Uniform is the NATO alphabet word for U

explanation.surface: A duty was imposed on the day the school dropped its uniform policy.
explanation.walkthrough: DEBUT without its U leaves DEBT.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money owed, a financial duty one is bound to repay.

indicators.note: a shower scatters things in all directions, so the letters come down in a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' looks like a wash but works as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn vow, a sworn undertaking to do or tell something.

clue.text: Wish to include 6 — play regularly with feeling

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of play

explanation.surface: An instruction to a musician: wanting to fit in number six, play it now and then with emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6-down, but it is simply the number written as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something lovingly means doing it with affection and tender emotion.

parts.note: to crawl is to swim front crawl, so crawled gives swam
the setter refers to themself as I; 'to' attaches it

explanation.surface: A holy man crawled over to where the crossword setter sat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawled' suggests creeping on hands and knees; here it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, a holy man devoted to spiritual mysteries.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: of the electrical crackle that disrupts radio reception

explanation.surface: Something that keeps disrupting a signal, as if a radio were still crackling.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means unmoving, and static electricity produces the crackling interference heard on radios.

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the step word wraps around the hospital letter

parts.note: a tread is the flat part of a stair you step on
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone stands outside a hospital holding a piece of lace.
explanation.walkthrough: TREAD wraps around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A lace is a cord or string, which is a kind of thread used for fastening or sewing.

parts.note: surface reading: a theatre advertising a show with that title
setter's reading: a drama whose mood swings up and down between sorrow and laughter

explanation.surface: A poster outside a theatre announcing a show called Emotional Rollercoaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title is not a real play; it describes a genre that mixes tears and laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragicomic drama blends tragedy and comedy, so the audience's feelings rise and fall like a fairground ride.

indicators.note: after says the plant word follows the turning word, giving the order of the two parts

parts.note: a U-turn is a change of direction
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A baby named Heather was swapped after someone did an about-face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a girl's name, but it is the plant, also called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a changeling is a fairy child secretly left in place of a stolen human infant.

clue.text: An Indonesian mammal related to birds

parts.note: the bat is a flying mammal
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: A zoologist describes an Indonesian creature with bird-like relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Batavia was the Dutch colonial name for Jakarta, so a Batavian is a person from there.
explanation.definitionFit: Batavia was the old colonial capital of the Dutch East Indies, now Jakarta, so its native is Indonesian.

clue.text: Fear can account for some secrets

indicators.note: for some means only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the three words, skipping the outer ones

explanation.surface: Anxiety explains why some people keep secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside feAR CAN Account.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcana are mysteries or hidden knowledge, things known only to the initiated.

indicators.note: sounding means what is heard rather than what is written, so the word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: coarse means rude or vulgar

explanation.surface: A passage of text that reads as vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: COARSE and COURSE are pronounced the same in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a route or way through, as in the course of a river or the passage of time.

clue.text: In Spanish port, sailor becomes fresh

parts.note: taken as written
Vigo is a port in north-west Spain
a rating is a sailor without officer rank

explanation.surface: A sailor in a Spanish harbour is revived by the sea air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition placing the sailor, but it is a piece of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh air is invigorating: bracing and energising.

clue.text: It's upsetting having cancelled green activity

parts.note: a match that is cancelled is off
putting is what golfers do on the green

explanation.surface: It is annoying when your round of golf is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests environmental activism, but it is the golf green.
explanation.definitionFit: Something off-putting is disconcerting or discouraging, leaving one disturbed.

parts.note: surface reading: the moment a taut situation finally tips over
setter's reading: the drink that leaves a tipsy person falling over drunk

explanation.surface: The critical moment when tension finally breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight is slang for drunk, and tipping is literal: the extra drink makes a person keel over.
explanation.definitionFit: Having had one drink beyond your limit is the familiar phrase for being drunk.

clue.text: Result of exams — wow, first in English!

parts.note: finals are the last exams of a degree course
cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of the following word only

parts.note: the opening letter of English

explanation.surface: A student cheers at getting a first-class mark in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Result of exams' reads as one phrase, but 'Result' alone is the definition. Cor is a British exclamation like 'wow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A final score is the outcome of a match, the result when play ends.

clue.text: Cost of fish, say, on the rise

parts.note: the char is a fish related to trout

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up, turning the short word around

parts.note: e.g. is short for for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: The price of fish is going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks an example, abbreviated EG, which reads upward in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is the price demanded for goods or a service.

indicators.note: unopened means the beginning is never reached, so the opening letter is removed

parts.note: the present time is now
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A wrapped gift left behind by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests a gift, but it is the present time, NOW; without its first letter it is OW.
explanation.definitionFit: The owl is a nocturnal bird of prey.

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and changes means it is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a marriage is a union of two people

explanation.surface: A trade union boss shifts his stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union leader' reads as a trade unionist, but 'leader' is the first letter of the word for union, whose M gives way to C.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is the way a person holds their body, their bearing when standing or walking.

indicators.note: away means sent off, so that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A ship that departed at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, and port fits that picture, but the answer is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is a container for holding liquid or food, which is what vessel means.

parts.note: to lace a shoe is to fasten it securely
a ration is a fixed allowance of supplies

explanation.surface: An order to slash spending and lock up provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: A laceration is a jagged wound or tear in the flesh.

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Someone declares their passion for eating a particular element.
explanation.walkthrough: Love meaning nil in tennis scoring gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine is a chemical element, a halogen with atomic number 53.

parts.note: perfect in the sense of complete, utter
fare is food, as in simple fare

explanation.surface: A recipe for cooking the ideal meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A way to perfect food' reads as cooking advice; 'A way' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a main road or route, a public street for travel.

clue.text: Prison reformer excited by hangover cure

parts.note: Elizabeth Fry was a famous English prison reformer
up means lively or stirred up

explanation.surface: A campaigner for prisoners is thrilled by a remedy for the morning after.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth Fry was a 19th-century Quaker who reformed British prisons; a fry-up is a British cooked breakfast of fried eggs, bacon and sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: A greasy cooked breakfast is the traditional British remedy after a night of heavy drinking.

wordplay.note: the two-word shout of a footballer wanting the ball passed over, run together

explanation.surface: A student asks for a reading list that will help them pass.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a player calling for a pass shouts 'To me!'; written as one word that is a big book.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy volume, usually a scholarly one.

parts.note: surface reading: a dishonest, untrustworthy person
setter's reading: a style of printing type whose letters slope

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark about someone of doubtful honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright type' suggests a person of good character; here type is printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic lettering slants to the right, unlike roman typeface, which stands vertically.

clue.text: Head of yellow flower absorbed by swelling tree

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken inside, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: a sore is a painful swollen spot

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of yellow
a flower in crosswords is often a river, a thing that flows; the Cam runs through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A yellow bloom is swallowed by a growth on a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' looks like a bloom but means something that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large maple tree with winged seeds.

clue.text: With change of pole, kinetic energy produces volatile spring

indicators.note: kinetic means in motion, so the letters are set moving into a new order
the poles are north and south, so one of those compass letters is exchanged for the other

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physics remark about energy and magnetic poles creating an unstable source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinetic energy' reads as a physics term, but kinetic is the anagram signal; ENERGY with N swapped for S becomes ESERGY before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that erupts violently and unpredictably.

clue.text: Cope, say, having a way with words

parts.words: Cope, say, having a way with words
parts.note: surface reading: someone who manages to get by thanks to being articulate

parts.words: Cope, say, having a way with words
